content.user_title: Govern Data Resources for Asset Readiness
content.value_statement: Scattered data lacks ownership, quality evidence, and consistent classification. This skill applies DCMM-based methods to create practical governance plans and deliverables.
actual_capabilities: Assess governance maturity across the eight DCMM capability domains and identify priority gaps.
Define scoped data inventory fields and a three-level resource catalog structure.
Create owner, steward, and custodian accountability matrices for governed data.
Design business terms, data element standards, metadata inventories, and lineage requirements.
Classify data using GB/T 43697-2024 concepts and define handling expectations.
Plan quality rules, lifecycle controls, governance procedures, and delivery checks.
limitations: The skill provides advisory drafts, not official DCMM certification or regulatory approval.
Assessments depend on complete evidence from business, technology, security, and data owners.
It cannot inspect databases, systems, or lineage automatically without supplied information.
Legal, accounting, valuation, and licensed assurance decisions require qualified professionals.

use_cases.title: Scope an asset-readiness program
use_cases.description: Define a focused governance scope, inventory plan, deliverables, responsibilities, and schedule for data intended for accounting, valuation, or exchange.

use_cases.title: Evaluate DCMM maturity
use_cases.description: Structure evidence collection across eight capability domains, score current practices, identify gaps, and prioritize a practical improvement roadmap.

use_cases.title: Build auditable governance artifacts
use_cases.description: Draft catalogs, responsibility matrices, classification tables, quality rules, metadata requirements, and lifecycle procedures for review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a data inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me scope a data inventory for [business area]. List required inputs, interview roles, inventory fields, and first-week deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a responsibility matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an owner, steward, and custodian matrix for [data domains]. Define decisions, operating duties, approvals, evidence, and escalation paths.

prompt_templates.title: Assess DCMM maturity
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our evidence against DCMM eight domains. Show assumptions, provisional scores, evidence gaps, priority risks, and a phased improvement roadmap.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced team conducting a maturity review

prompt_templates.title: Design an asset-readiness governance program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design governance for [data assets] supporting [accounting, valuation, or exchange]. Integrate cataloging, lineage, classification, quality, ownership, controls, acceptance criteria, and handover.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced program design across governance workstreams

output_examples.input: Our customer data spans CRM, billing, and support systems. What should we inventory first?
output: Scope: customer master, contact, contract, billing, and service records.
Evidence: system owners, table lists, update frequency, usage, sharing, and retention.
Priority: records supporting revenue, customer obligations, reporting, or external use.

output_examples.input: How should responsibility be assigned for product master data?
output_examples.output: Assign a business owner for policy, a steward for definitions and quality, and a custodian for technical controls. Name accountable roles and evidence.

output_examples.input: What should a DCMM gap summary contain?
output_examples.output: Include domain scores, cited evidence, missing controls, business impact, target maturity, accountable owners, recommended actions, dependencies, and review dates.

best_practices: Start with data tied to a defined business outcome and document the scope boundary.
Support every maturity score, classification, and ownership decision with named evidence.
Have business, technology, security, legal, and finance stakeholders review relevant deliverables.
anti_patterns: Do not launch an enterprise-wide program before agreeing priorities, boundaries, owners, and acceptance criteria.
Do not assign accountability only to departments; name specific roles with decisions and duties.
Do not treat governance completion as automatic approval for accounting, valuation, or exchange.

faq.question: Does this skill certify DCMM maturity?
faq.answer: No. It structures a self-assessment and improvement plan. Formal certification requires an authorized assessment process.

faq.question: Can it create a data resource catalog?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define the hierarchy, fields, responsibilities, and review rules when you provide system and business details.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide policies, system inventories, metadata, lineage, quality reports, access controls, ownership records, issue logs, and representative business use cases.

faq.question: Does governance make data ready for accounting recognition?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Governance supports evidence, but accounting recognition also requires compliant control, identifiability, and reliable measurement.

faq.question: Can it classify confidential data?
faq.answer: It can propose classifications and handling requirements. Security, legal, and business owners must validate the result against current obligations.

faq.question: Can it connect to our databases?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides methods and document drafts from supplied information. It does not automatically access systems or extract metadata.
